## Start with the offline tutorial

Load an installed current development version with `library(scAgentKit)`.
Copy the steps below into an R session and inspect each saved review before
approving it. Chunks are not evaluated during the build because approval is an
interactive analyst action. The example needs no API key, data download or
optional algorithm package.

This example uses the public SeuratObject `pbmc_small` counts (230 genes,
80 cells). The mock supplies fixed software-control settings and `Unknown`
annotations. It makes no network request. These settings are for learning the
workflow, not for choosing parameters for a study.

```{r tutorial}
source(system.file("examples", "researcher-pbmc.R", package = "scAgentKit"))
project_dir <- file.path(getwd(), "pbmc-tutorial")  # choose a new directory
mock <- make_researcher_pbmc_mock()
run <- researcher_pbmc_start(project_dir, mock)

view <- researcher_pbmc_inspect(project_dir)
view$strategy_review$details
researcher_pbmc_decide(project_dir, view, reviewer = "analyst",
  reason = "Reviewed the tutorial settings and retained-cell scope.")
run <- researcher_pbmc_resume(project_dir, mock)

view <- researcher_pbmc_inspect(project_dir)
view$strategy_review$details$cluster_diagnostics
researcher_pbmc_decide(project_dir, view, reviewer = "analyst",
  reason = "Reviewed the measured resolution comparison; retain this software control's 0.4, without claiming an optimal resolution.")
run <- researcher_pbmc_resume(project_dir, mock)

view <- researcher_pbmc_inspect(project_dir)
view$annotation_review$details
researcher_pbmc_decide(project_dir, view, reviewer = "analyst",
  reason = "Reviewed markers; keep tutorial identities unresolved as Unknown.")
done <- researcher_pbmc_resume(project_dir, mock)
stopifnot(identical(done$status, "complete"))
final_object <- readRDS(done$output$seurat)
done$output
```

Each approval records a decision about the saved proposal. Resume performs the
approved work and stops at the next review step. Inspect a fresh snapshot after
changing a proposal. The tutorial helpers wrap the same `sc_run()`,
`sc_run_inspect()`, `sc_run_review()` and `sc_run_resume()` used for real projects.


## Inspect and reopen

```{r reopen}
view <- sc_run_inspect(project_dir)
view$status
view$output
# Optional, using installed resources with an existing Python >= 3.9:
sc_open(project_dir)
```

The viewer reads saved results without continuing analysis. Keep the same R
implementation and library for later computation. `complete` records execution;
it does not establish biological correctness of the tutorial labels.

## Continue with your own study

Use genuine raw counts and verified study metadata, or explicitly declare a
processed-Seurat entry with a reuse reason. Review study-specific QC, PC,
clustering and annotation choices rather than copying the tutorial settings.
Model assistance is optional and requires separate aggregate-transfer consent.

The repository's [documentation index](https://github.com/ChanghaoKan/scAgentKit/blob/main/docs/README.md)
links the complete researcher guide, current strategy and annotation contracts,
optional methods and browser instructions. Installed API help is available with
`help(package = "scAgentKit")`.
